findings.bible: Render targets section: 'RenderTarget2D support ... needed a real type-safety fix when sampling a render target back as an ordinary texture.'
findings.target: modules/renderers/webgpu/include/CNA/Internal/Renderers/WebGPU/WebGPURenderer.hpp::IWebGPUSamplable (View() plus REMED-GFX-167 Sampled()) implemented by WebGPUTextureRenderer and WebGPURenderTargetRenderer; modules/renderers/webgpu/src/WebGPURenderer.cpp::ResolveSamplable (dynamic_cast, nullptr/'unbound' for an incompatible type). Header comment: before RenderTarget2D existed every GpuDrawParams::textureN was a WebGPUTextureRenderer and every Queue*Draw used an unchecked static_cast; WebGPURenderTargetRenderer cannot derive from WebGPUTextureRenderer (diamond over ITextureRenderer), so a small interface mirrors VulkanRenderer's IVulkanSamplable.
findings.site_now: absent: webgpu-renderer-semantics.html#cube-targets explains only the cube sibling (IWebGPUCubeSamplable); no page mentions IWebGPUSamplable, ResolveSamplable or the old static_cast hazard for plain 2D targets.

fix.html: The cube interface has an older 2D twin. IWebGPUSamplable (View() plus Sampled()) is implemented by both WebGPUTextureRenderer and WebGPURenderTargetRenderer. Before RenderTarget2D existed, every texture a draw could name was a WebGPUTextureRenderer, so each Queue*Draw() stored it through an unchecked static_cast; a render target is an unrelated class (both derive from ITextureRenderer, so one cannot inherit the other without a diamond), which turned that cast into a real hazard. ResolveSamplable() replaces it with a dynamic_cast that treats a null or incompatible resource as unbound, the same shared-capability-by-small-interface pattern the Vulkan renderer uses.

findings.bible: What remains open: WebGPU queries were an open gap; the site closes it with 'records a real begin and end pair around its draws and resolves an exact sample count'.
findings.target: modules/renderers/webgpu/src/WebGPURenderer.cpp::ReplayDrawsInOrder: 'only a query's FIRST run this flush is recorded, since a query slot may be written just once per resolve -- the same policy VulkanRenderer applies' (recordedThisFlush_), so draws split by other draws or by a later pass are not counted. ::AllocateOcclusionSlot: kMaxOcclusionSlots = 32; when every slot is in use the query 'never records' (slot_ = -1, replay and readback skip it, IsComplete stays false). modules/renderers/webgpu/examples/webgpu_occlusion_query_test.cpp asserts only PixelCount == 0 for an occluded quad and PixelCount > 0 ('near a full 64x64 target') for a visible one, never an exact number; WebGPUOcclusionQueryRenderer does not override PixelCountIsPreciseEXT (inherited default true, no device probe).
findings.site_now: webgpu-renderer-semantics.html#pipeline-state: 'resolves an exact sample count'; 132-webgpu.html#capabilities: 'resolve an exact sample count'; native-gpu-evidence-tiers.html#identities: 'real, exact sample count' (the same table qualifies VULKAN with 'first contiguous run only'). No page mentions the first-run rule or the 32-query pool.

fix.old_html: CreateOcclusionQuery() returns a query that records a real begin and end pair around its draws and resolves an exact sample count.
fix.html: CreateOcclusionQuery() returns a query that records a real begin and end pair around its draws and resolves the samples that pass depth and stencil. Only a query's first contiguous run of draws in a flush is recorded (a query slot is written once per resolve, the policy the Vulkan renderer also applies), the renderer owns a fixed pool of 32 query slots so a 33rd live query never records or completes, and WebGPU_OcclusionQuery checks zero for a fully occluded quad and a positive, near-full-target count for a visible one, not an exact number.

fix.old_html: Real begin/end queries that resolve an exact sample count.
fix.html: Real begin/end queries counting the samples that pass depth and stencil (the test distinguishes zero from a near-full count; no exact count is asserted). Only a query's first contiguous run of draws per flush is recorded, and at most 32 query objects can be alive at once.

fix.old_html: real, exact sample count
fix.html: real; first contiguous run per flush only; 32 query slots

findings.site_now: 105-browser-renderers.html#what-they-emit: 'In all three cases SDL3 still owns the real <canvas> element -- it stays in the layout, hidden ... The DOM and SVG renderers create their own surface over the top of it.' fix.old_html: In all three cases SDL3 still owns the real <canvas> element — it stays in the layout, hidden, because SDL keeps sizing it and delivering input through it. The DOM and SVG renderers create their own surface over the top of it.
fix.html: In all three cases SDL3 still owns the real <canvas> element and keeps sizing it and delivering input through it. CANVAS draws straight into that canvas's 2D context, so it stays visible. HTML_DOM and SVG_DOM build their own surface over the top of it and leave the canvas in the layout at opacity: 0 (transparent, deliberately not visibility:hidden or display:none, so it stays the hit-test surface for SDL's input handlers); its original opacity is restored at teardown.

fix.html: MSAAExactly one mode: 4× (a standard four-sample pattern). A request of 4 or more applies 4× (the source comment: XNA asks for the greatest supported count no larger than its preference, so an 8 clamps to 4), and a request below 4 applies as none — the applied count is what gets reported back, not the one you asked for. GDI's CPU MSAA is stricter: only an exact 4 enables it.
